findings: The entire corrected English body matches Cummiskey AP214, printed p. 203. The original-resolution image confirms commas after sins and sight. Those commas were absent in early packet 3083fab4 and have been restored in the accepted v2 bytes.

Author and governor renders institutor et rector; deliver them from the sins by which they are assaulted preserves the force of peccata, quibus impugnatur, expelle. English plural they/them refers naturally to the people expressed collectively in the Latin.
Always explicitly renders semper. Well pleasing in thy sight and safe under thy protection preserve both requested outcomes. Lowercase thy and the literal Thro’. abbreviation are retained.
Cummiskey prints only the Latin incipit Populi, not the full Latin prayer. Full Latin comparison uses target no. 731 at CMAA AP195/p114 and Mame AP258/p144, both personally inspected.

The actual Thursday heading is Cummiskey AP211/p200; its Postcommunion is at AP213/p202 and this prayer is at AP214/p203 before the Friday heading. Target Thursday begins at CMAA AP193/p112; AP194/p113 supplies its Postcommunion and Super populum cue before the prayer on AP195.

Let us pray, Bow down your heads to God, PRAYER and Populi are source labels/cues outside the selected prayer body. Thro’. is an authentic abbreviated ending, not a certification of a supplied full English conclusion.

findings: The complete English body matches the Lasance AP271/p271 donor, including lowercase almighty, wonted mercy, Thou dost permit confidently to rely, and the short Through our Lord. conclusion.

Be present to our supplications preserves the opening petition. The reordered request for the effect of wonted mercy preserves consuetae misericordiae tribue benignus effectum, while those whom Thou dost permit confidently to rely on Thy goodness renders quibus fiduciam sperandae pietatis indulges without omitting its beneficiaries or confidence in divine goodness.

The complete target at CMAA AP205/p124 no. 794 has the same words and short Per Dominum. The Lasance parallel Latin has a colon after indulges where target and Mame have a semicolon; this pointing difference is declared and changes neither petition nor English meaning.

The exact held donor is lent-2-monday/main/Oratio super populum/all/1. Complete canonical Latin including punctuation, wraps and final LF equals the candidate. The complete English entry equals the packet donor object, and the source passage resolves to the exact matching English at tracked carrier line 70.

The donor page precedes the actual Tuesday heading despite the Tuesday running header. It does not attest the recipient appointment. The recipient Passion Wednesday heading is independently visible at CMAA AP203/p122; no. 794 follows its Postcommunion and Super populum cue on AP205 and precedes the actual Thursday heading.

Mame AP216/p102 supplies the exact Monday donor prayer and short ending. No longer same-day ending or saint-name addition has been substituted. The separate Humiliate/Bow down cue and Concluding Prayers direction are excluded from the body.
